newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris stocks dive as Europe bubbles higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris stocks dive as Europe bubbles higher.

text.p: European stock markets followed Wall Street into record territory on Wednesday with the exception of Paris where investors' election worries sent the bourse into a dive.

The French stock market fell two percent in early trading with traders saying investors were wary ahead of Sunday's election runoff following the strong Socialist showing in the first round. That compared with fresh trading highs hit in Germany, Hong Kong, Australia, Austria, Spain and Amsterdam after Wall Street's record close on Tuesday night when the Dow Industrial Average ended up 0.51 percent at 7,383.41.
The dollar began European trade mixed, steady against the mark but softer against the yen after a rise in Japanese government bond yields and a 2.32 percent surge in Tokyo share prices.
Platinum and palladium prices also soared to fresh highs on news of an illegal strike in South Africa, the world's largest platinum producer.
Palladium, platinum's sister metal, surged to a high of $188.00 per ounce compared to a fixing on Tuesday afternoon of $177.50.
"The market has gone crazy. The market is very, very tight," said one dealer following a wildcat strike at Anglo American Platinum Corp's Rustenburg mine which cut output by 15 to 20 percent.
Although German government bonds, or bunds, and British gilts firmed in early trading, the main focus in Europe was on stock markets.
With the Paris CAC-40 down just over two percent by 0930 GMT, one trader said: "Most people are hesitant to be long in this market," a trader said.

Dealers said President Jacques Chirac's televised appeal to voters on Tuesday urging them not to weaken France's voice in the runup to monetary union by electing an opposition government did not have much impact on the market.
In contrast to Paris, Germany's 30-share DAX index pushed to a new trading high in early trade and within sight of the psychologically important 3,700-point level.

"Wall Street was up yesterday and it looks like we're trying to emulate that good order flow here. This is not a down day and I think it's very possible that we could break 3,700 points today," said a Frankfurt broker.
Among individual stocks insurance giant Allianz advanced 6.7 marks to 382.50 after a positive 1997 outlook.

London investors were also cheered by Wall Street's strong performance, but analysts said the market may not have the momentum to carry the blue chip FTSE 100 index into new ground immediately because of worries about rising bond yields.

"The market makers have pushed up prices once again this morning but I don't think we'll see a lot of buyers," the head of sales and trading at a major investment bank said. "The market is looking a bit toppy."
The FTSE 100 was up 11 points to 4,692.6 by 0930 GMT but off its highs.
Calling the top of either the Dow or the FTSE has proved to be difficult in recent weeks as both indices have been trading at or near record levels.

"Common sense tells you that this can't go on forever. But as long as interest rates stay low, shares will be attractive and there is still no clear sign that rates are about to soar," one senior London dealer said.
On the currency front, analysts said that while higher Japanese bond yields and the jump in the Nikkei had helped to boost the yen against the dollar, its gains were seen as limited.

"What is most likely to happen is that dollar/yen will stabilise around where it is now. Looking at it from a wider perspective, we expect it to settle around 115-118 yen," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.
By 0930 GMT the dollar was trading at 116.03 yen against 116.50 in late Europe on Tuesday. Against the mark, the dollar was steady at 1.7038 against 1.7005 on Tuesday.
Stagliano said dollar/yen was unlikely to re-visit five-month lows below 112 yen seen last week unless Japanese authorities gave it a helping hand.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7038 marks and 116.30 yen compared with 1.7005 marks and 116.50 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 11.0 points, or 0.23 percent, at 4,692.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 53.94 points, or 2.01 percent, at 2,626.40.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 6.03 points, or 0.16 percent, at 3,680.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Palladium fixed at a record $188.00, compared with $177.50 on Tuesday afternoon after news a strike in South Africa.
Platinum fixed at $404.50, highest since August 1996, while gold was slightly firmer at $345.10, up $1.35. Silver was two cents stronger at $4.77.
